body.text:
Final gate r0076 met my unchanged criteria version 1: 113/128 fresh task episodes, zero hardware violations, with a 95% Wilson interval of 81.6–92.8%. White-like plugs succeeded 65/70 times and black-like plugs 48/58 times. All 128 exact CPU replays reproduced the gate stages and hardware outcomes. The successful videos show active opposed-finger reorientation and a held blades-up finish; the failed example loses the plug during the turn.

What worked: the full reconstruction hour produced a VALID reference with all ten quality checks passing, while preserving hidden-frame invalidity and monocular uncertainty. Physical rolling solved the contact problem that rigid two-pad retargeting could not. Matching CPU/GPU geometry and controllers made PPO training useful. A compact neural reference plus PPO state feedback transferred better than direct imitation. Lower-rate neural endpoint decisions, interpolation and a final neural-target hold made the strict final-second stability reward learnable. Training from actual deployment handoffs improved the learned skill.

What failed: locked-contact retargeting penetrated by about 6–7.5 mm; small supervised errors in both direct and masked behavior cloning compounded into bad rollouts; constant 50 Hz exploration prevented terminal settling. Extra PPO checkpoints were rejected when their paired gains were inconclusive. An earlier-hold counterfactual worsened a replayed failure, so it was not kept. Rare abduction-joint snapback remains: the selected policy had nine velocity violations in a separate 4096-state catalog diagnostic, versus eighteen for the neural reference. Wider placement proposals succeeded only 18/32 times; combined wider changes succeeded 20/32 times.

The claim is limited to this declared simulation and conditioned grasp distribution. Object identity and contact parameters remain estimated, perception is idealized except for encoder noise, and exact human joint/axis imitation and real-hand transfer are not demons…
